Brainspotting

I used my finger to direct my gaze slowly around the field of vision to see how different memories felt, or what memories came up, at different angles. That was basically how I figured out very quickly that I could do a simple version myself.

I had heard the claim that when you move your eyes to the top left you are remembering and the top right you are thinking or constructing something. That simple map did not hold up when I checked it, so I do not use it to read other people's eyes.

I like Brainspotting because it makes it easy to do something like edging. I did not know if that was the right word. What I mean is going in and out of the uncomfortable spot and kind of feather-touching the boundary rather than jumping straight into the deep end. It feels more effective to me.

And I give it so many more points because it is democratic like EFT. You do not need an expensive expert just to experiment with a simple version, although you can get one too. I would not take that as an invitation to jump into the deepest trauma alone.

EMDR

Brainspotting, as I understand it, is something you can do yourself. I have done it myself. It is intuitive, and you can figure it out quickly. EMDR is more targeted toward specific memories or traumas, with recall procedures and so on. Brainspotting you can feel out, and it does not require knowing exactly what you are targeting.

Shaking Qigong / Shaking Medicine

I mean what energy is stuck in you. I often have the kind of natural shaking that animals have, rather than noticing much benefit from intentional therapeutic techniques. Especially on psychedelics, it is like my body knows exactly which part to shake and how. So it is not just “shaking = mental health.” It is more like this: when the right thing is shaken the right way, things loosen up as they should and the energy flows.

TRE is a system people are trying to teach en masse, so they had to distill the method down to what seems to work most of the time for most people. But obviously, if you could get more angles at it, you would get more chance of success—and less chance of being called an expert, lol. “Just try lots of stuff till it works” is how my expertise runs on this.

I did not try the Shaking Qigong class, but I have done qigong and it was very helpful in moving energy. I can understand how the two would naturally go together. I can also see how it might be a middle ground between fully predictable TRE structure and totally unstructured shaking. That would probably suit more people who need some guidance but cannot benefit from standard TRE. It is also social, and that can work better than individual practice for many people when they see others getting results.

I still need to be able to stop, orient, and settle afterward. If not, that is not the right dose.
